# Filing a plan or work that runs for a while

For plans, migrations, releases, rollouts, refactors, setup steps, and for
debugging, incidents, background jobs and CI watching. The rules in `SKILL.md`
still apply.

## Checklist

- One `task` per step, added `open` in the order you will do them. The step you
  start is `in_progress` with a `note` ("Backfilling: 1.2M of 4M rows").
- A step that needs consent is an ask on that step. Work for someone else is a
  `task` owned by `{"kind":"other","name":"N"}` that says who and what.
- As you go, update the note with `item.edit` (patch `{"note":"..."}`), close each
  step `done` with its result and start the next. The tree is the checklist; the
  owner watches "In progress". Closing a step ends its note.

## Live work

- The work is a `task`, `in_progress`; its `note` is the one line the owner sees in
  the tree, so keep it current.
- Each hypothesis or lead is a child `finding`: `done` when confirmed, `dropped`
  with why when ruled out. The root cause is a `finding`; follow-ups are tasks.
- When the work ends, close the task with what happened, and add a summary item
  if the owner needs a report (`report.md`).

## Example

A plan whose first step has started, a consent ask on the second and a step for
someone else.

